target_only_tests.note: Seven cases, none counted as ported coverage. Every one was measured red under a named mutation and green again on revert (docs/test-translation-conventions.md rule 10); the probe ids are C1..C8 and the measurements are quoted here and in the per-entry reasons above. `a float literal is not an integer, however round it looks` (C1: answering the int question from the VALUE -- `typeof x === "number" && Number.isInteger(x)` -- instead of from the document turns it red, `expected PyValueError to be thrown, but nothing was thrown`). This is rule 9's most consequential instance in this belt and the reason the loader parses with `pyJsonLoads`: `1.0`, `1e2`, `1E2`, `6.0e1` and `-0.0` are all `float` to Python's `json.loads` and all refused by `isinstance(value, int)`, and all five are ordinary integers to `Number.isInteger`. A `cooldown_sec: 1e2` that interlock refuses would have loaded silently, and the refusal message names the type the DOCUMENT wrote (`got float`), which is `type(value).__name__` exactly. `an integer literal spelled with a leading minus is still an integer` is the complement, and it is here so the int check cannot pass by refusing everything: a plain integer literal has to reach the NON-NEGATIVE guard rather than the type guard, and the two produce different sentences. C8 (removing the non-negative guard) turns it red along with two ported cases. `a notify or template kind naming an Object.prototype member is not inherited` and `a config document keyed by an Object.prototype member is read as data` are rule 9's other family: the attention kind is a caller-supplied string used as a map key, Python's `dict` has no inherited keys, and on an object literal `cfg.notify["constructor"]` answers with a function -- a severity nobody configured, for a kind nobody wrote. `__proto__` needs the second case of its own because it fails in the opposite direction: assigning it on a literal SETS THE PROTOTYPE and stores nothing, so the one kind the operator configured is silently absent while every other kind in the same document loads fine. C2 (both maps built as `{}`) turns both cases red. Note also what that case's own FIXTURE had to change: the document is written as JSON text rather than through `JSON.stringify` of an object literal, because a `__proto__` key in a literal sets the prototype there too and the fixture would have shipped a document that never carried the key under test. `a template key present with a null value is refused, not defaulted` (C3: `template["title"] ?? ""` turns it red) -- `tmpl.get("title", "")` defaults only on an ABSENT key, and the case asserts both halves so the fix cannot be to refuse an absent one too. `the sound refusal prints the modes in sorted order` (C4: listing the modes in declaration order turns it red, `expected 'config.sound must be one of ['off',...' to be '...['all',...'`) -- the source builds the message from `sorted(_VALID_SOUND_MODES)` over a frozenset, so the printed order is sorted and not declaration order, and the whole message is what an operator reads to fix their file; the ported case checks only the substring `config.sound`. `the placeholder allowlist is the design's six names` (C5: dropping one name turns it red) -- nothing in A2 READS this set, because `notify.render_text` is A3's, so without a case here the constant could be emptied or misspelled and the whole sub-belt would stay green.

notes: `approved_non_running` is empty because the file uses no non-running construct. Checked directly against scripts/parity-check.mjs's own NON_RUNNING patterns -- `(test|it|describe).skip`, `(test|it|describe).todo`, `(test|it).fails`, `skipIf(` and `xfail(` -- over test/attention/config.test.ts with comments and string literals INCLUDED, which is stricter than the sweep: no match. The source has no capability gate to carry and the port adds none. `conditionally_collected` is empty for the same reason: all 34 mapped ids plus the 7 target-only ones were present in `vitest list --json` when this ledger was written (41 collected from this file, 41 passed).

ALL 34 ARE `ported` AND NONE IS `adapted`, which is worth defending rather than leaving to look like an oversight, because `PORTING_LEDGER.md` classes `attention/config.py` itself as `rewrite`. That classification is about the MODULE's fate in interlock's own successor -- its knobs are keyed to a vocabulary interlock is replacing -- and it is not a statement about what a translation of its test file may assert. Case by case, nothing here reads a different fact or asserts a different property from its source: the constructor is `__post_init__`, the loader is `load_config`, the refusal messages are byte-identical to the source's for every input a case supplies, and the field names differ only by `D-0201`'s camelCase rule, which no ledger in this port has ever counted as an adaptation. The two places where the port's MECHANISM differs -- the integer check and the two map constructions -- are described in the notes below and are pinned by target-only cases; neither changes what a ported case reads or asserts, which is the line this port's other ledgers draw (see parity/session.stub-provider.ledger.json's note on the same question).

THE RULE 9 ANSWERS, which `docs/test-translation-conventions.md` requires in the porting report. (1) WHICH CALLER-SUPPLIED STRINGS ARE USED AS A MAP KEY: the attention kind, in `notify` and in `templates`, on both the loader's write path and every consumer's read path. Both maps are built with `Object.create(null)`, and `DEFAULT_NOTIFY` already was (A1, `D-0902`), so all three severity/template maps in the module agree. The loader's own presence tests over the DOCUMENT use `Object.hasOwn` rather than `in` for the same reason, though that half is defensive rather than measurable: none of the fourteen top-level JSON keys collides with an `Object.prototype` member, and the target-only case says so instead of implying a measurement it did not make. (2) WHICH `number` PARAMETERS THE SOURCE TYPES `int`: all ten of the JSON integer knobs, and the answer is the document-spelling check described in the next note rather than a `Number.isInteger` guard.

`isinstance(value, int)` IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE DOCUMENT, NOT ABOUT THE VALUE, and that is why this loader parses with `pyJsonLoads` and asks `pyTypeNameOf`. Python's `json.loads` produces an `int` only for a literal with no `.`, `e` or `E`; `1.0` and `1e2` are floats and are refused. Both reach the same `number` in this runtime, where `Number.isInteger` says yes to each, so the obvious guard accepts two shapes interlock refuses -- and it also cannot produce the message, because `type(value).__name__` is `float` for values that are integral here. `pyJsonLoads` records the spelling the source text used and `pyTypeNameOf` reports `int` or `float` from it, which is the same question and the same answer; `bool` and `str` fall out of the same call. This is the port's existing CPython transcription (`src/fencing/pyjson.ts`, `src/fencing/pysemantics.ts`), already shared by `src/settings/` and `src/session/`, not a second local rendering.

ONE DIVERGENCE IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN GUARDED, because guarding it would be the divergence. Python's `int` is arbitrary-precision, so a document writing `cooldown_sec: 12345678901234567890` loads that exact value; this runtime rounds it to the nearest double, and `pyTypeNameOf` still answers `int`, so the value is accepted and carried rounded. Refusing it would make the port narrower than its source for an input the source handles. Nothing observable follows from the rounding here: every one of the ten knobs is a threshold compared against an age in minutes or seconds, and both readings of a value above 2**53 are the same unreachable threshold. Recorded so a later consumer that does ARITHMETIC on one of these knobs -- rather than a comparison -- knows the claim it can and cannot make.

WHAT REPLACED `__dataclass_fields__`, since the source reads its own defaults back out of it. `load_config` needs four default values (`pending_decision_max`, `pending_decision_drop`, `user_replied_min`, `pending_decision_min`) to decide whether a legacy document's TTL ladder needs auto-scaling, and it reads them from the dataclass rather than repeating the literals. A TypeScript class carries no such record, so the defaults are named once in an exported `ATTENTION_CONFIG_DEFAULTS` and BOTH the constructor and the loader read them from there. The alternative -- literals in the constructor and a second set in the loader -- would reintroduce exactly the drift `__dataclass_fields__` was avoiding, in a place where the two copies disagreeing means a legacy config either fails to load or is scaled against a threshold nobody uses.

THE TWO CONSTANTS THAT NOTHING IN THIS SUB-BELT READS, named so a reviewer can see they were considered. `ALLOWED_PLACEHOLDERS` is consumed by `notify.render_text`, which is A3's; it is carried here because that is where the source keeps it, and it is pinned by a target-only case because an unread constant is otherwise free to rot. `SoundMode` has one consumer, the loader's own validation, and `Template` has one, the loader's construction -- both exercised by ported cases.

WHAT A1 LANDED AND A2 DID NOT TOUCH. `D-0902` required A2 to FILL THIS FILE IN rather than replace it, and its falsifier was A2 having to CHANGE it. `Severity` and `DEFAULT_NOTIFY` are byte-identical to what A1 landed, including the `Object.create(null)` construction and the frozen wrapper; the only edit above them is the module header, which A1 wrote to describe an A1-shaped file and which now describes the finished one. Recorded here rather than left to the diff, because "A2 changed A1's file" is the observation D-0902's falsifier asks a reviewer to look for, and a header rewrite is not it.
